title: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve Brief Note
summary: A concise official profile of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve in the national tiger conservation context.
useFor: Use as a quick orientation before reading full planning, legal, and compliance documents.
researchNote: Good for high-level reserve facts, but do not treat it as a substitute for notifications, plans, or sanction records.

title: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve Notification
source: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
summary: Official Gazette notification related to the Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve eco-sensitive zone context.
useFor: Use for legal basis, notified details, regulated activity context, and compliance interpretation.
researchNote: This is a primary legal source. Cite the Gazette notification rather than a secondary summary when making legal or policy claims.

title: Tiger Conservation Plan - Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve (Earlier Archive)
source: WII MEE-TR portal / Rajasthan Forest Department
summary: Earlier archived long-form planning document for reserve management, protection, habitat, prey, tourism, eco-development, and monitoring priorities.
useFor: Use for management background and comparison with newer TCP material that includes the Bhainsrodgarh core-addition context.
researchNote: Useful for management questions, but read alongside the newer TCP archive where Bhainsrodgarh is noted as a 2023 core addition.

title: Tiger Conservation Plan - MHTR with Bhainsrodgarh Core Addition
type: Core management plan / updated official copy
source: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve / Rajasthan Forest Department
summary: Newer official TCP archive that states Bhainsrodgarh Sanctuary was added to Mukandra Hills Tiger Reserve by order 4854336 dated 05.10.2023 and made part of the core tiger reserve.
useFor: Use for the current Bhainsrodgarh core-addition context, updated management framing, corridor notes, protection infrastructure and long-form planning details.
researchNote: This is the key source for the Bhainsrodgarh update. It is large; open in a dedicated tab when reading maps, annexures or tables.

title: Annual Plan of Operation 2019-20 - MHTR
summary: Operational and financial planning record for Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve for the 2019-20 cycle.
useFor: Use for budget heads, approved actions, implementation priorities, and annual management intent.
researchNote: Compare APO line items with field outcomes and later sanction documents to understand continuity or gaps.

title: NTCA Sanction Order - Rajasthan 2024
summary: Recent NTCA sanction document for tiger reserve work in Rajasthan, useful for tracking funded priorities and current-cycle conservation support.
useFor: Use to understand sanctioned priorities, funding direction, and current-cycle management support.
researchNote: Read alongside reserve-specific APOs and implementation reports; sanction does not by itself prove field completion.

title: Management Effectiveness Evaluation Technical Manual - Tiger Reserves in India
summary: NTCA technical manual explaining the Management Effectiveness Evaluation framework used for tiger reserves in India.
useFor: Use for understanding MEE terminology, evaluation criteria, management-effectiveness context and how tiger reserves are assessed.
researchNote: This is not MHTR-specific, but it helps readers understand official management evaluation language used across tiger reserves.

title: Zonal Master Plan for Eco-sensitive Zone of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: Zonal planning document for the eco-sensitive zone context around Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve.
useFor: Use for zoning logic, permissible activity interpretation, land-use compatibility, and planning controls.
researchNote: Important for development-pressure analysis around the reserve; pair with legal notifications and local planning records.

title: Notified ESZ Document - Rajasthan Tiger Reserve Section
summary: A compact Rajasthan Forest Department PDF covering ESZ and tiger reserve reference tables, including Mukundara.
useFor: Use for quick ESZ and reserve-area reference across Rajasthan tiger reserves.
researchNote: Useful as a compact table source, but cite full notifications and ZMP documents for detailed compliance work.

title: Wildlife Clearance File - Bharatmala NH-148N Section near MHTR
summary: Wildlife conservation / clearance file for a highway section in the wider Mukundara-Darrah landscape context.
useFor: Use for mitigation commitments, project conditions, and wildlife-clearance context around infrastructure proposals.
researchNote: The conditions and mitigation sections are critical; they define obligations after approval.

title: Reptiles and Amphibians of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: A field guide-style reference focused on reptiles and amphibians recorded in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve.
useFor: Use for non-mammal baseline context, field identification support, and biodiversity education.
researchNote: A useful counterweight to tiger-only narratives; verify taxonomy against current sources when needed.

title: Phytodiversity Characterization of Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
source: International Journal of Current Microbiology and Applied Sciences
summary: Research article on plant diversity characterization in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve.
useFor: Use for sampling design, plant diversity records, and habitat interpretation.
researchNote: Review methods and sampling effort before using headline diversity claims.

title: Status of Wildlife between Kota Barrage and Jawahar Sagar Dam, Rajasthan
summary: A WII rapid assessment report on aquatic wildlife and river habitat quality along the Chambal River stretch between Kota Barrage and Jawahar Sagar Dam.
useFor: Use for Chambal river-valley context, otter signs, crocodile and turtle records, waterbirds, raptors, fish diversity, and development-impact interpretation around the wider Mukundara landscape.
researchNote: This report can contain sensitive field locations. Use it for ecological context and citation, but avoid republishing precise nest, roost, or wildlife-use coordinates.

title: Caracal Comeback in Ramgarh Visdhari and Mukundara Hills
summary: Open-access natural history note documenting the first photographic record of caracal from Ramgarh Visdhari and Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserves.
useFor: Use for caracal distribution, rare small-cat conservation context, camera-trap monitoring value and semi-arid western Indian landscape interpretation.
researchNote: The article includes camera-trap maps and record context. Cite the finding without republishing precise wildlife-use locations.

title: Record of Cinereous Vulture from Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: Short communication reporting a Cinereous Vulture sighting from Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve during a February-March 2015 prey-status study.
useFor: Use for vulture occurrence, scavenger records, raptor context, and evidence that MHTR supports more than tiger-focused conservation values.
researchNote: The article includes field context and a precise observation locality. Cite the record, but avoid amplifying sensitive location detail unnecessarily.

title: Occupancy and Habitat Use of Sloth Bear in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve
summary: Study of sloth bear occupancy, signs, den records and habitat use in Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve, with mixed forest and water-adjacent habitats highlighted.
useFor: Use for sloth bear distribution, habitat preference, sign-survey context and human-use pressure around MHTR.
researchNote: The paper discusses bear signs and den habitat. Use the ecological findings carefully and avoid turning site-specific records into visitor guidance.

title: Sloth Bear Diet in Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve
source: International Journal of Research and Analytical Reviews
summary: Research article on sloth bear food availability and scat-based diet composition in Darrah Wildlife Sanctuary, part of the Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve landscape.
useFor: Use for sloth bear feeding ecology, seasonal food context, plant-food references and insect-heavy diet interpretation.
researchNote: Treat the percentages as study-specific results from sampled scats, not as a complete diet profile for every season or part of the reserve.

title: Dietary Composition of Leopard in Mukandara Hills National Park
source: International Journal of Pure and Applied Bioscience
summary: Scat-analysis study of leopard diet in Mukandara Hills National Park, recording prey items such as Hanuman langur, jackal, nilgai, fox, wild boar and domestic dog.
useFor: Use for leopard prey context, historical carnivore ecology and comparing prey-base notes with later MHTR management documents.
researchNote: The paper uses an older protected-area name and a small scat sample. Cross-check with newer monitoring data before making broad prey-base claims.

title: Kali Sindh River - Vibrant Ganga Biodiversity Brief
source: Wildlife Institute of India / Ganga Knowledge Portal
summary: A river-basin brief for the Kali Sindh, including land-cover, river-system and biodiversity context for the basin that passes through Darrah Wildlife Sanctuary in MHTR.
useFor: Use for Kali Sindh basin context, riverine biodiversity, fishing cat and otter habitat references, and wider Chambal-linked landscape interpretation.
researchNote: This is a concise brochure, not a full technical report. Pair it with detailed river, wetland and protected-area studies for analysis.

title: Wildlife Corridors of Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve
source: International Journal of Education, Modern Management, Applied Science & Social Science
summary: Research paper focused on wildlife-corridor significance for Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve and wider biodiversity conservation.
useFor: Use as a secondary corridor-context source, especially when discussing connectivity, gene flow, landscape permeability and conservation planning.
researchNote: Treat as a research reference rather than a legal or management notification. Cross-check corridor claims against official plans and GIS sources.

title: Lok Sabha Answer - Genetic Inbreeding in Tiger Sub-Populations
summary: Government answer on tiger sub-population inbreeding, connectivity, Project Tiger implementation and corridors involving Ranthambore, Kuno, Madhav and Mukundra.
useFor: Use for official parliamentary wording on tiger connectivity, genetic-inbreeding concerns and inter-reserve corridor policy context.
researchNote: This is a policy-answer source. Use scientific studies and corridor assessments alongside it for ecological interpretation.

title: Status of Tigers, Co-predators and Prey in India 2022
source: NTCA and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: National tiger-estimation report covering tiger status, landscapes, co-predators, prey, habitat connectivity, camera-trapped sites and conservation implications.
useFor: Use for national and landscape-scale context around tiger monitoring, co-predator/prey assessment and connectivity framing relevant to MHTR.
researchNote: This is broad national context and includes sensitive survey information. Use it for interpretation, but avoid extracting precise camera or wildlife-use locations.

title: Global Tiger Protected Area Compendium
summary: Large comparative compendium for tiger protected areas across the tiger range.
useFor: Use for broad comparative framing against other tiger landscapes.
researchNote: Informative for context, not a replacement for Mukundara-specific planning records.

title: Mukundara Hills Tiger Reserve Notification, 2013
summary: The base Rajasthan notification declaring 417.17188 sq km as Critical Tiger Habitat and 342.82274 sq km as buffer, totalling 759.99462 sq km.
useFor: Use as the historical legal baseline for MHTR core, buffer and total area before the 2023 amendment.
researchNote: The filename mentions ESZ, but the document is the 2013 tiger-reserve notification. Read it separately from the final 2020 ESZ Gazette.

title: MHTR Core and Buffer Amending Notification, 2023
summary: The amendment revising MHTR to 690.71178 sq km of Critical Tiger Habitat and 445.07522 sq km of buffer, totalling 1,135.787 sq km.
useFor: Use for the current state-government legal area and the Bhainsrodgarh core-addition context.
researchNote: The Forest Department link currently exposes a one-page scan whose table continues beyond the visible page. Use the published area figures with the current protected-area register and updated Tiger Conservation Plan; do not infer an unseen full schedule.

title: Rajasthan Long Term Action Plan for Tiger Conservation
fileName: Long term action plan Final Updated maps.pdf
issued: Approved 6 Oct 2023; maps updated through Oct 2023
summary: Statewide tiger-conservation action plan that records an in-principle proposal for further MHTR core and buffer additions and sets out conditions before notification.
useFor: Use for proposal status, connectivity and management priorities; keep proposed additions separate from the notified reserve area.
researchNote: The MHTR proposal is not itself a boundary notification. The plan records further consent, State approval and statutory steps.

title: Management Effectiveness Evaluation of Tiger Reserves in India, 2022 — Fifth Cycle
source: National Tiger Conservation Authority and Wildlife Institute of India
summary: The fifth-cycle national MEE report, including MHTR's 60.16 percent score, Good rating and dated management observations.
useFor: Use for the conditions documented during the 2022 evaluation, management strengths, recommendations and comparable national methodology.
researchNote: The observations are a dated evaluation, not a live statement of conditions in 2026. Later evidence should be checked for each issue.

title: NTCA Rajasthan Annual Plan Sanction, 2025–26
summary: Rajasthan's FY2025–26 tiger-reserve approval and first-instalment sanction, including the MHTR programme and release calculation.
useFor: Use for approved budget heads and management intent in FY2025–26.
researchNote: Approval or fund release does not prove expenditure, completion or ecological outcome; follow-up evidence is required.

title: CAG Chapter IV: Management of Tiger Reserves in Rajasthan
source: Comptroller and Auditor General of India
summary: Subject Specific Compliance Audit chapter on Rajasthan tiger-reserve management for FY2016–17 to FY2020–21, with later position updates identified in the report.
useFor: Use for dated, system-level accountability themes such as staffing, protection, invasive species, land security, relocation and participation.
researchNote: Do not assign statewide or multi-reserve findings to MHTR alone, and do not present historical audit findings as verified current conditions.

title: Rajasthan Human–Wildlife Conflict Ex-Gratia Order, 2026
summary: State order revising ex-gratia amounts and procedure for human death, permanent incapacity and injury caused by wildlife.
useFor: Use for current compensation amounts, eligibility conditions and process; verify the live Forest Department record before filing a claim.
researchNote: The order sets ₹10 lakh for death or permanent incapacity, ₹2 lakh for grievous injury and ₹25,000 for minor injury, subject to its certification and procedural conditions.

title: Rajasthan Voluntary Village Relocation Package Amendment, 2025
fileName: GoR 24.07.2025 land package modification new Final.pdf
summary: Order replacing the 2022 land-package provisions and confirming a choice between the prescribed land package and ₹15 lakh cash—or the then-applicable NTCA amount—per displaced family.
useFor: Use for current package options while assessing consent, rights settlement, eligibility, land, services and livelihood outcomes.
researchNote: Relocation from protected areas must be described as voluntary and rights-based; a package announcement is not evidence of consent or completed rehabilitation.
